bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price risk - exposure to plastic resin and agricultural commodity prices with no effective hedge — The Company's businesses remain exposed to fluctuations in prices of key raw materials, particularly plastic resins and certain agricultural commodities. Since effective hedging mechanisms for plastic resins are not available, it can only monitor market movements and adjust procurement, pricing and inventory strategies; PVC resin swings during FY2026 drove channel inventory rationalisation and cautious dealer procurement.
- Liquidity and working-capital risk — Liquidity management is explicitly listed among corporate-level risks. The Company relies on a disciplined approach to operating cash flow and working capital efficiency - retail-led model, cash-and-carry sales, improved collections, inventory optimisation and prudent capital allocation - and reports that it continued to meet all debt servicing obligations and maintained its borrowings as 'Standard' with all lending institutions.
- Receivables and collection risk, especially under Government-supported programmes — Timely recovery of receivables, particularly under Government-supported programmes, remains an important focus area. Mitigation is a deliberate shift towards the retail-led business model and cash-and-carry sales while reducing dependence on project-based business, backed by dealer relationships and disciplined credit management.
- Climate change and weather risk — Changing climatic conditions, erratic rainfall patterns, extreme weather events and increasing pressure on water resources continue to impact agricultural activity and demand across the Company's businesses - the same forces that also create demand for its climate-smart irrigation and water-management solutions.
- Demand risk tied to agricultural activity, Government policy and infrastructure spending — Demand across businesses is influenced by agricultural activity, Government policies, infrastructure spending, rural income levels and overall economic conditions, making the order profile dependent on programme implementation; the Company leans on its MIS, extensive dealer network and market intelligence to track requirements.
- Geopolitical and global economic risk — Geopolitical developments, changing international trade policies, reciprocal tariff measures, supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures and global economic uncertainty may impact both domestic and international operations; diversification and global presence are the stated mitigants.
- Interest rate and foreign exchange risk — Domestic and international operations expose the Company to interest rate and currency movements; it uses treasury management practices including forward exchange contracts where considered necessary, alongside a continued focus on cash flows and working capital.
- Capacity utilisation risk — Utilisation across businesses may be influenced by seasonal demand, Government programme implementation, customer demand patterns and overall market conditions; the Company works to improve it through product diversification, retail expansion, export growth, value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations.
- Agri-input supply and crop-cycle risk in Agro-Food Processing — The food business faces unpredictable weather, changing crop patterns, inflationary pressures, agricultural commodity price fluctuations, rising logistics and supply chain costs, and availability of quality agricultural produce; mitigation runs through the integrated farm-to-fork model, contract farming and a diversified sourcing network.

outlook.body: The main capacity addition disclosed for FY2026 was in the Agro-Food Processing business run through Jain Farm Fresh Foods Limited (JFFFL), where the Company successfully commissioned two high-speed bottling lines for juices and carbonated soft drinks for one of India's leading beverage companies, resulting in a significant expansion of its private label and contract manufacturing business; management states the commissioning of these new beverage bottling facilities further strengthened manufacturing capabilities and expanded the Company's presence in the growing private label and contract manufacturing segment. JFFFL's footprint spans manufacturing facilities and business operations across India, Turkey, Belgium, the United Kingdom and the United States, serving food manufacturers, food service companies, institutional buyers, retail chains, private label brands and co-manufacturing partners. Going forward the Company says continued investments in innovation, manufacturing capabilities, private label solutions and operational excellence are expected to further strengthen its competitive position, and it remains committed to enhancing productivity across the value chain and improving processing efficiencies. In plastics, expansion is described qualitatively rather than as projects: in PVC Sheets/WPC the Company intends to strengthen its presence by introducing value-added products, expanding market reach and enhancing customer engagement on the back of established manufacturing capabilities and an expanding distribution network. Management also flags capacity utilisation risk - utilisation across businesses may be influenced by seasonal demand, Government programme implementation, customer demand patterns and market conditions - and says it continues to improve utilisation through product diversification, expansion of the retail business, export growth, introduction of value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations. No rupee capex outlay, dated project pipeline or plant-wise capacity table is disclosed in this section.

outlook.body:
- Government focus on rural drinking water through the Jal Jeevan Mission, plus PMAY, AMRUT, Swachh Bharat Mission, PMKSY and irrigation expansion, is expected to provide sustained demand for plastic piping
- Stabilisation of PVC resin prices and gradual normalisation of channel inventories, together with improving demand from agriculture, housing and infrastructure, are expected to support recovery in the domestic plastic piping business
- Increasing replacement demand, growing awareness of BIS-certified products and rising adoption of modern plumbing systems are expected to provide further growth opportunities
- HDPE adoption driven by water supply investment, irrigation, city gas distribution network expansion, wastewater treatment and industrial infrastructure; superior strength, flexibility, corrosion resistance and long service life support substitution away from steel and concrete
- PVC Sheets and Wood Polymer Composite demand supported by urbanisation, residential and commercial construction and a shift toward lightweight, durable, moisture-resistant and recyclable building materials replacing wood, plywood and metal
- Agro-Food Processing outlook supported by changing consumer preferences, demand for processed and convenience foods, focus on food safety and traceability, expansion of organised retail and food service, and India's position as a large producer of fruits, vegetables and spices with cost-competitive manufacturing
- Hi-Tech Agri was the growth engine, with segment margins over 18% described as among the best in precision agriculture globally, and the shift towards retail, exports, value-added products and cash-and-carry business gathering pace
- Tissue culture demand demonstrated by a single day's dispatch of 1,253,191 banana plantlets; the innovation pipeline includes new variety introductions Jain Sweet Orange-6 and Jain Mandarin-1
- Dehydrated Ingredients Division recorded one of its best years in three decades; the fruit business held volumes and profitability even as softer farm-gate prices lowered reported realisations
- Overseas plastics: Ex-cel Plastics held a strong position in European PVC foam sheets, UK and Ireland operations served building products, packaging, storage systems and technical plastics, and the addition of Harlequin extended reach into wastewater treatment, rainwater harvesting and storage
- Headwind: unseasonal rainfall affected crops and demand in several markets, and the domestic piping business bore the brunt of PVC resin price swings, cautious dealer stocking and slower infrastructure execution
- Watch-item: the IMD forecast the southwest monsoon at 90% of the Long Period Average, signalling early stress for India's farm economy and raising food-security concerns
- Watch-item: continuing global conflicts and looming disruptions to supply chains and logistics put pressure on day-to-day working of the Company
- Received a ₹135 crore order for 5,438 solar agricultural pumps under Maharashtra's solar pump programme, following successful execution of the earlier phase
- Completed subsea execution of India's largest single HDPE marine intake pipeline for the Perur site of Chennai's 400 MLD desalination plant, adding to a portfolio that already includes the Minjur desalination plant
- Commissioned and inaugurated the Gendoli-Folai Lift Irrigation Project in Rajasthan, which will irrigate around 4,000 hectares and benefit close to 25,000 farmers across 17 villages using solar power

risks.risk: Raw material price risk - exposure to plastic resin and agricultural commodity prices with no effective hedge
risks.note: The Company's businesses remain exposed to fluctuations in prices of key raw materials, particularly plastic resins and certain agricultural commodities. Since effective hedging mechanisms for plastic resins are not available, it can only monitor market movements and adjust procurement, pricing and inventory strategies; PVC resin swings during FY2026 drove channel inventory rationalisation and cautious dealer procurement.

Liquidity management is explicitly listed among corporate-level risks. The Company relies on a disciplined approach to operating cash flow and working capital efficiency - retail-led model, cash-and-carry sales, improved collections, inventory optimisation and prudent capital allocation - and reports that it continued to meet all debt servicing obligations and maintained its borrowings as 'Standard' with all lending institutions.

risks.risk: Receivables and collection risk, especially under Government-supported programmes
risks.note: Timely recovery of receivables, particularly under Government-supported programmes, remains an important focus area. Mitigation is a deliberate shift towards the retail-led business model and cash-and-carry sales while reducing dependence on project-based business, backed by dealer relationships and disciplined credit management.

Changing climatic conditions, erratic rainfall patterns, extreme weather events and increasing pressure on water resources continue to impact agricultural activity and demand across the Company's businesses - the same forces that also create demand for its climate-smart irrigation and water-management solutions.

risks.risk: Demand risk tied to agricultural activity, Government policy and infrastructure spending
risks.note: Demand across businesses is influenced by agricultural activity, Government policies, infrastructure spending, rural income levels and overall economic conditions, making the order profile dependent on programme implementation; the Company leans on its MIS, extensive dealer network and market intelligence to track requirements.

Geopolitical developments, changing international trade policies, reciprocal tariff measures, supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures and global economic uncertainty may impact both domestic and international operations; diversification and global presence are the stated mitigants.

risks.risk: Interest rate and foreign exchange risk
risks.note: Domestic and international operations expose the Company to interest rate and currency movements; it uses treasury management practices including forward exchange contracts where considered necessary, alongside a continued focus on cash flows and working capital.

Utilisation across businesses may be influenced by seasonal demand, Government programme implementation, customer demand patterns and overall market conditions; the Company works to improve it through product diversification, retail expansion, export growth, value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations.

risks.risk: Agri-input supply and crop-cycle risk in Agro-Food Processing
risks.note: The food business faces unpredictable weather, changing crop patterns, inflationary pressures, agricultural commodity price fluctuations, rising logistics and supply chain costs, and availability of quality agricultural produce; mitigation runs through the integrated farm-to-fork model, contract farming and a diversified sourcing network.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jain Irrigation Systems Limited (JISL) is a well-diversified, integrated player offering solutions in sustainable agriculture, water management and food processing, with a global reputation as an agriculture and irrigation technology leader.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: JISL operates across three business verticals: Hi-Tech Agriculture Solutions (micro and sprinkler irrigation systems, tissue culture, planting material and solar agri pumps), Plastic Piping Systems (PVC and PE pipes for agriculture, infrastructure and plumbing applications) and Agro Processing (through its subsidiary Jain Farm Fresh Foods Limited and overseas subsidiaries in the UK, USA, Belgium and Turkey). It is the world's largest producer of tissue-cultured banana and pomegranate plants, India's largest producer of polyethylene (PE) pipes and among the top three manufacturers of PVC pipes in the country. The Company also works in renewable energy, hybrid seeds, biogas solutions, bio-fertilizers and precision agriculture, serving customers across more than 120 countries.

- Agro-Food Processing outlook supported by changing consumer preferences, demand for processed and convenience foods, focus on food safety and traceability, expansion of organised retail and food service, and India's position as a large producer of fruits, vegetables and spices with cost-competitive manufacturing
- Hi-Tech Agri was the growth engine, with segment margins over 18% described as among the best in precision agriculture globally, and the shift towards retail, exports, value-added products and cash-and-carry business gathering pace

- Commissioned and inaugurated the Gendoli-Folai Lift Irrigation Project in Rajasthan, which will irrigate around 4,000 hectares and benefit close to 25,000 farmers across 17 villages using solar power

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- World's largest producer of tissue-cultured banana and pomegranate plants, with annual capacity exceeding 120 million banana tissue culture plants
- India's largest producer of polyethylene (PE) pipes and among the top three PVC pipe manufacturers in the country
- Diversified, integrated portfolio spanning Hi-Tech Agri Input Products, Plastic Piping and Agro Processing, which cushions segment-specific downturns
- Global reach with customers in more than 120 countries and revenue spread across India, Europe, North America and Rest of World
- Long-term relationships with key vendors that enable it to contain raw-material cost increases to some extent and ensure steady supply
- Cash-and-carry business focus, with dealers booking orders by paying advances, supporting cash flows through periods of resin price volatility

- Expand exports and value-added businesses while continuing to improve collections and working-capital efficiency
- Make significant repayments of long-term debt in FY2027 to strengthen the balance sheet further; focus on free cash generation, collections, prudent investment and profitable growth while finance costs remain high
- Invest in climate-smart irrigation, biotechnology, disease-resilient planting material, protected cultivation, digital farming, …
